summary.intent: Run discuss-phase for Phase 21 (BYO-IPFS Node Support) to capture implementation decisions about auth token security, pinning model, settings UI, and provider compatibility before planning begins.
summary.outcome: CONTEXT.md created at `.planning/phases/21-byo-ipfs-node-support/21-CONTEXT.md` with decisions that significantly depart from the original requirements — client-direct pinning becomes v1.1 (not v1.2), pinning mode is user-configurable (not always-dual), and TEE handles pin migration as a background job.

repo: The original PROJECT.md plan of 'server-relay for v1.1, client-direct v1.2' was reversed during discussion — the SDK's existence makes client-direct the natural v1.1 approach, with the server never relaying IPFS operations.
BYO-IPFS credentials should be stored as vault metadata on IPFS (encrypted with user's key), not in the server DB — preserving the zero-knowledge model already established for vault content.
The TEE (Phala Cloud + BullMQ) already handles background jobs like IPNS republishing and can handle pin migration the same way — it never needs plaintext, only opaque encrypted blobs and CID lists.
CipherBox API role in BYO-IPFS is narrowed to: IPNS publishes, DB mutations, and advisory quota tracking only — no server-side pinning relay.
Pinning mode becomes user-configurable: CipherBox only (default), external only, or dual-pin — determined after SDK-level benchmarking rather than prescribed upfront.
STATE.md contained an open concern about BYO-IPFS auth token storage that needed to be resolved before gray area discussion could proceed.

code.finding: Existing provider interface that the new RemotePinningProvider will implement — SDK-layer extension point for BYO-IPFS.
Reference implementation for the provider pattern; RemotePinningProvider will follow the same structure.
Existing settings page where BYO-IPFS configuration UI (endpoint, auth token, pinning mode selector, connection test, migration status) will be added.
Pinned CID entity may need a field to record which node(s) a CID is pinned to, supporting migration status tracking.
Original BYO-IPFS spec (BYO-01 through BYO-07) — the acceptance criteria still apply but the pinning model and auth storage approach differ from what was originally specified.

workflow: discuss-phase correctly surfaced a conflict between STATE.md's open concern and the stated architecture, prompting a scope/model clarification before any gray areas were selected.
The discuss-phase workflow allowed a mid-discussion architectural pivot (server-relay → client-direct) to be captured cleanly without scope creep — the change was to the HOW, not the WHAT.

friction: STATE.md had an unresolved open concern about auth token storage that wasn't fully resolved in prior phases, requiring it to be addressed at the start of this session rather than as a gray area.

The original PROJECT.md architecture (server-relay v1.1) conflicted with the zero-knowledge design principle already established for vault content — this inconsistency required explicit discussion before gray areas could be framed correctly.
open_items: SDK-level benchmarking of RemotePinningProvider with external IPFS providers (Pinata, web3.storage, etc.) needed before deciding which pinning modes are viable long-term.
TEE pin migration job: client provides CID list + source/destination configs (auth tokens encrypted with TEE public key); TEE handles fetch-pin-verify cycle and reports progress to DB.
Settings UI migration status display — show per-CID or aggregate progress when user switches pinning modes.
Advisory quota tracking approach finalized (CID registration only, no enforcement) but the DB schema changes to support it are deferred to planning.
Provider compatibility matrix (which external providers support standard IPFS Pinning Service API vs requiring custom adapters) — deferred to research phase.
